subject.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids

question: Should this PR intentionally fail closed when lsof emits malformed PID records in `gateway --force` and stale gateway cleanup, even if that can stop an existing cleanup path instead of proceeding?
rationale: The diff chooses safety over permissive parsing for malformed OS-tool output; automation can verify the code path, but maintainers own the compatibility and operator-experience tradeoff.

options.title: Accept fail-closed cleanup
options.body: Merge with the explicit tradeoff that malformed lsof PID output errors or waits rather than truncating a token and possibly signaling the wrong process.

options.title: Request live gateway proof
options.body: Ask for a real `gateway --force` or restart-cleanup transcript before merge if maintainers want end-to-end evidence beyond parser-level terminal proof and CI.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics only
options.body: Reject the cleanup-path behavior change and keep only the non-destructive diagnostics hardening if fail-closed cleanup is too risky for this release.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed cleanup
recommendation.body: Merge with the explicit tradeoff that malformed lsof PID output errors or waits rather than truncating a token and possibly signaling the wrong process.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned, requested review, and authored the final fail-closed commit on this PR.
